text:
RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 5

You and the successful candidate are both women, so sex cannot plausibly explain why she was chosen over you. An all-female panel says nothing here except perhaps something about who works in education. Raising it would weaken your credibility on the point that actually matters.

That point is strong: on the published facts you appear better qualified for a leadership post — a master's in educational leadership and five years actually doing deputy principal work, against "courses" and classroom experience. Ask again in writing for the reasons, note the two-week silence, and request the assessment criteria and how each candidate was scored against them. Build your case on qualifications and process, not panel composition.
